A1.justification: Both 69-page PDFs describe the same NTK-Attention research. Their text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: V1 reports original approximation-error experiments, ChatGLM3-6B evaluations on SuperGLUE, and ViT fine-tuning results on CIFAR-100 and Food-101.

after.justification: V2 reports original language and vision evaluations, additional math evaluations, and an empirical runtime and parameter-count comparison.

M1.justification: The core attention computation using trainable Z and k remains. V2 Appendix C adds an optional low-rank parameterization Z = Z_A Z_B with specified initialization, changing the trainable representation. The PDFs do not establish that this extension was used in the reported experiments.

E1.justification: V2 adds mathematical reasoning through MetaMathQA training and GSM8K/MATH evaluation, substantially extending the task coverage beyond language understanding and image classification. It also adds Tiny-ImageNet while retaining the original SuperGLUE, CIFAR-100, and Food-101 coverage.

E2.justification: The retained vision comparison expands from full fine-tuning alone to include LoRA at ranks 16 and 32. V2 also evaluates Zero-Shot in the math comparison and standard Prefix Attention in the computational-cost study. The original SuperGLUE comparator families remain.

E3.justification: V2 introduces MetaMathQA supervised fine-tuning of Llama-3.2-1B/3B, with LoRA ranks 16/32, and a CPU timing protocol varying input and prefix lengths. SuperGLUE Table 1 adds P-Tuning V2 with m=200. These are added evaluation settings; the shared optimizer, epochs, batch sizes, and precision settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V1 Section 4.4 tests approximation error across prefix lengths up to 2^18; this analysis is removed. V2 Appendix B.2 instead investigates runtime and parameter-count scaling across prefix and input lengths. The added m=200 SuperGLUE row also extends prefix-length sensitivity evidence.

E5.justification: The removed approximation study reports 50 repetitions and displays error bars. The new runtime study reports 10,000 repetitions with maximum, minimum, and mean values. These concern different experiments, not an increase in repetitions of the same experiment. The retained benchmark tables keep their existing plus/minus reporting convention.

E6.justification: Reported NTK vision accuracy changes from 91.69 to 92.55 on CIFAR-100 and from 89.70 to 90.57 on Food-101. Original SuperGLUE rows remain unchanged, while the added m=200 row averages 65.36 versus 69.37 at m=100. Math, Tiny-ImageNet, vision-LoRA, and runtime results are added; the approximation-error results are removed.

T1.justification: The main convergence theorem and most appendix proofs remain substantively unchanged. V2 adds scaling-law Proposition 3.3 and revises the approximation theorem to require bounded prefix-derived keys/values and Equation (7). It also corrects the matrix Chernoff upper-tail inequality and removes v1 Appendix J's auxiliary scalar-gradient derivations.

C1.justification: V1's introduction claims pretraining-independent convergence on any dataset. V2 replaces this prominent claim with convergence for a simplified, sufficiently overparameterized attention setting, and its abstract explicitly describes the setting as stylized. The stated empirical contributions also expand to math reasoning and measured computational efficiency.

C2.justification: V2 newly discusses the unfactorized method's parameter disadvantage relative to LoRA, compatibility with LoRA, and unresolved relationships between prefix length and reasoning complexity. Appendix C adds a CoT/o1 interpretation. The earlier general experimental limitations and reasoning-skill discussion are largely retained.

D1.justification: V2 Section 4.2 explicitly supplies the implemented feature map with r=d and the Z/k update rules. Appendix B.2 documents the new benchmark's initialization, dimensions, and AMD CPU execution. The shared training configuration and code-access URL remain unchanged; these disclosures do not establish changes to retained experiments.

R1.justification: V2 substantially refocuses the literature discussion through a new theory-of-LLMs overview covering efficient computation, white-box transformers, and emergent abilities, plus CoT positioning in Appendix C. It adds scaling-law and math-benchmark literature while removing much of the activation-function and hierarchical-learning background.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, theoretical setup, and method derivation are extensively rewritten. Related work becomes Section 1.1, the contents move to the front, references move before the appendices, and the appendices are reorganized to begin with algorithms, experiments, and discussion. The title and author block also change.

P2.justification: V2 adds a method schematic, math-result bar charts, and a runtime plot with an inset, while removing the approximation-error plot. It introduces side-by-side algorithms and detailed appendix algorithm boxes. The vision table gains comparator rows, a dataset column, and averages; the SuperGLUE table gains the m=200 row.

improvement.justification: V2 makes the stylized theoretical scope and implementation easier to assess and strengthens empirical comparisons through vision LoRA baselines and math evaluations. These gains provide a limited net improvement. They are partly offset by removing the direct approximation-error study and leaving new inconsistencies unresolved: m=200 underperforms m=100 despite the increasing-prefix narrative, and the quadratic-runtime claim conflicts with the stated complexity at fixed input length.
